articles.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama notches 43 points on career-best 34 shots in win
articles.description: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points on Saturday to propel a 121-111 win over the Timberwolves.
articles.headlineJa: スパーズのビクター・ウェンバンヤマ、キャリア最多の34本を放ち43得点を記録し勝利に貢献
articles.descriptionJa: スパーズのスター、ビクター・ウェンバンヤマが土曜日、キャリア最多となる34本のシュートを放ち、シーズン最多の43得点を記録。チームをティンバーウルブズへの121-111の勝利に導いた。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points on Saturday to propel a 121-111 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.

"When he plays with his teammates, it really causes a problem for the other team, whether that's spacing, handling the basketball, playing two-man game or three-man game" Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "The best players in this league, when they play with their teammates, it's damn near impossible at times [to stop]. You've got to just choose how they beat you. He's made some fine improvement in a short amount of time."

Wembanyama's performance marked the first time the Spurs emerged victorious on a night the Frenchman finished with 30 attempts or more. The 22-year old also contributed 5 blocks to become the first Spur since David Robinson (1996) to rack up at least 40 points and 5 blocks in a game, and the first player since Joel Embiid (2022) to accomplish the feat.

San Antonio fell short the two previous times Wembanyama hoisted 30 shots or more. He attempted 31 shots on Christmas Day of his second NBA season (2024) to finish with 42 points in a 117-114 loss to the New York Knicks. Four days later, Wembanyama finished with 30 attempts in a 112-110 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

"He's just so dominant," said second-year guard, Dylan Harper, who notched a regular-season career-high 25 points on 9-of-17 shooting. "When he puts his imprint on the game, he's unstoppable. He did that tonight from the jump to the end of the game."

Wembanyama's shot diet looked different, too. He nailed a corner 3-pointer with 2:40 remaining for his final bucket to extend San Antonio's lead to 118-107. Wembanyama would fire up eight 3-pointers on the night, knocking down three of them.

But 12 of Wembanyama's 14 other baskets came from distances of two feet or fewer, including four alley-oops and four dunks. Wembanyama mentioned after struggling in San Antonio's season-opening loss to Oklahoma City that he needed "to go back to playing the basketball I like."

By the 5:23 mark of the third quarter, the "WemVP" chants started raining down on Wembanyama as he took a pair of foul shots.

"It's like pattern recognition," he explained. "The brain, after so many games, literally hundreds of games now in the NBA, knows what kind of game to go towards to have fun. Because whenever we don't score, it's like negative feedback. Whenever we score, we get good results, positive feedback for the brain. Over time, you recognize patterns, and you err towards those patterns. There's always ups and downs, but we're turning in the right direction."

San Antonio's four-guard starting lineup featuring Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Harper continues to make progress. Wembanyama, Fox, and Harper combined for 90 points as the Spurs won the rebounding battle 49-38. articles.headline: Boozer, Stewart lead Memphis to a 136-105 victory over Kings as Grizzlies remain unbeaten
articles.description: — Rookie Cameron Boozer had 27 points and nine rebounds, Isaiah Stewart added 24 points as the Memphis Grizzlies remained the only unbeaten team in the NBA with a 136-105 victory over the Sacramento Kings on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: ブーザーとスチュアートが活躍、メンフィスがキングスに136-105で勝利し無敗を維持
articles.descriptionJa: — 新人のキャメロン・ブーザーが27得点9リバウンド、アイザイア・スチュアートが24得点を挙げ、メンフィス・グリズリーズは土曜日の夜にサクラメント・キングスを136-105で破り、NBAで唯一の無敗チームを維持した。
articles.body:
MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- — Rookie Cameron Boozer had 27 points and nine rebounds, Isaiah Stewart added 24 points as the Memphis Grizzlies remained the only unbeaten team in the NBA with a 136-105 victory over the Sacramento Kings on Saturday night.


              The Grizzlies' 6-0 record matches the 2014-15 season for the best start in franchise history. After the Houston Rockets' 116-111 loss at Dallas on Friday night, Memphis was the last unbeaten team in the league. The Grizzlies dominated the Kings in the second half to coast home, with the lead reaching 34 in the second half.


              GG Jackson finished with 21 points, connecting on all five of his 3-pointers as Memphis built its lead in the first half. Cam Spencer, starting at point guard as Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. sat out with back issues, had 10 points and 13 assists.


              Meanwhile, the Kings, led by 38 points from Darus Acuff Jr., continue to struggle in the season's early stages, dropping to 0-6. Acuff, the rookie from Arkansas, scored 34 points against New Orleans in a loss Thursday, De'Andre Hunter finished with 19 points. Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine scored 11 points each, Sabonis adding 14 rebounds and eight assists.


              Memphis led by 21 points in the first half behind Jackson's 3-point shooting, but Acuff was able to keep the Kings into the game with 21 first-half points. The Grizzlies led a 66-55 lead at intermission as Jackson connected on all five of his 3-point attempts.


              The double-digit margin ballooned to 30 in the third quarter as Stewart and Boozer, the third pick in last summer's draft fueled the Memphis offense. The Grizzlies outscored Sacramento 42-25 in the third.


              Up next
              Kings: At Mavericks on Monday night.


              Grizzlies: Host Pelicans on Monday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Wembanyama has 43 points and 6 blocks to lead Spurs past short-handed Timberwolves 121-111
articles.description: — Victor Wembanyama had 43 points, seven rebounds, six blocks and four assists as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111 on Saturday night for their fourth straight victory.
articles.headlineJa: ウェンバンヤマが43得点6ブロックを記録、スパーズが戦力不足のティンバーウルブズを121-111で撃破
articles.descriptionJa: — ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマが43得点7リバウンド6ブロック4アシストを記録し、サンアントニオ・スパーズは土曜日の夜にミネソタ・ティンバーウルブズを121-111で下し、4連勝を飾った。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- — Victor Wembanyama had 43 points, seven rebounds, six blocks and four assists as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111 on Saturday night for their fourth straight victory.


              Dylan Harper added 25 points and six assists for San Antonio in the opener of a three-game homestand. De’Aaron Fox scored 20.


              Wembanyama was 17 of 34 from the field in reaching 40 points for the 10th time in the regular season and the 11th time in his career. After blocking Jonathan Kuminga’s 3-point attempt, Wembanyama raced downcourt for a two-handed dunk to give him 40 points.


              Ayo Dosunmu had 27 points and nine rebounds to lead the short-handed Timberwolves. Kuminga and Jaden McDaniels added 19 points apiece.


              Minnesota was without injured starters Anthony Edwards (knee surgery) and Rudy Gobert (back spasms). LaMelo Ball was limited to 20 minutes due to foul trouble.


              The Spurs opened the second half on a 13-4 run that included a fifth foul on Ball, who fouled out with 3:43 remaining. He finished with 10 points, eight rebounds, four assists and three steals.


              San Antonio grabbed a 43-33 lead after Wembanyama threw the ball off the backboard to set up his own layup, which was followed by Harper stealing the ensuing inbounds pass for a layup. 


              The Timberwolves went on a run shortly after Ball exited with 7:40 left in the first half after picking up his fourth foul. Minnesota responded by going on a 16-0 spurt to take a 51-46 lead. Kuminga and Dosunmu had five points apiece during the surge.


              Minnesota outscored San Antonio 33-26 in the second quarter, getting 10 points off five Spurs turnovers.


              Up next
              Timberwolves: Host the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday night.


              Spurs: Host the Utah Jazz on Monday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Jabari Smith Jr. scores 30 points, Rockets beat Thunder 119-98
articles.description: — Jabari Smith Jr. had 30 points and nine rebounds, Marcus Smart added 24 points and the Houston Rockets beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 119-98 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Jabari Smith Jr. had 30 points and nine rebounds, Marcus Smart added 24 points and the Houston Rockets beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 119-98 on Saturday night.


              Smith shot 10 of 18 from the field, including 6 of 12 on 3-pointers. Smart was 7 of 10 on 3s as the Rockets shot 46% as a team and were 18 of 41 from behind the arc.


              Alperen Sengun, who returned to the lineup after missing the last two games with lower back soreness, finished with 16 points, nine rebounds and 10 assists, and Kevin Durant scored 14 points.


              Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 26 points on 10-of-20 shooting, and Kenrich Williams and Bennett Stirtz scored 11 apiece for Oklahoma City, which lost its second straight after beginning the season 4-0.


              Isaiah Hartenstein and Jared McCain had 10 points each for the Thunder, which shot 44% and were 10 of 32 on 3s.


              Leading 37-30 a minute into the second quarter, the Rockets used an 18-4 run to open up a 55-34 lead on an Amen Thompson tip-in with 6:10 remaining in the half. Oklahoma City outscored Houston 17-8 over the final six minutes to cut the Rockets’ lead to 62-51 at the half.


              The Rockets opened the third with an 8-0 run to open up a 19-point lead on a 3-pointer by Smith with 10 minutes remaining in the quarter Houston’s lead never dipped below 12 the rest of the way.


              Fred VanVleet was out of the lineup due to right knee injury management, and Reed Sheppard missed his second straight game with low back soreness for the Rockets.


              The Thunder played their first game after announcing Friday that Chet Holmgren would miss at least two months because of a right knee injury.


              Up next
              Thunder: At Cleveland on Monday night.


              Rockets: Host Boston on Monday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick on Lamine Yamal: 'Easier' to substitute when he scores
articles.description: Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナのハンジ・フリック監督、ラミン・ヤマルについて：「彼がゴールを決めれば、交代させやすい」
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日にスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウで行われたラ・リーガのアラベス戦（6-1で勝利）で活躍したラミン・ヤマルについて、ハンジ・フリック監督は、彼がゴールを決めた後であれば交代させるのも容易だと語った。
articles.body:
Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.

Yamal netted a brace as Barça returned to winning ways after back-to-back defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

The teenager has now started all 18 games for Barça and Spain this season, although he was afforded a short rest against Alavés, with Flick able to take him off for the final 20 minutes with the game won.

"When you score two goals, it's easier to go out," Flick said after substituting Yamal for just the fourth time this season.

"I spoke with him at half time [about managing his minutes]. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half [is good], but it also important he has less minutes."

Barça opened the scoring early on through Raphinha before Fermín López added the second in the 23rd minute.

Raphinha's second of the game, and his 17th of the season, made it 3-0 and Yamal capped a fine team move with a brilliant finish from the edge of the box to make it four by half time.

Yamal netted another after the break, a dinked finish over the goalkeeper initially ruled out for offside, and Anthony Gordon scored the sixth late on prior to an even later consolation goal from Mariano Díaz.

It was just what Barça needed after a week which saw their 11-game winning run halted by losses to PSG in the Champions League and Madrid in the league.

"For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermín, Rapha," Flick added.

"This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way."

Flick also had praise for his makeshift defence, with midfielder Frenkie de Jong featuring at centre-back and youngster Brian Fariñas, also a midfielder, making his full debut at right-back.

"At the moment we have to think different," Flick said. "Four defenders are out in Xavi Espart, Andreas [Christensen], Jules [Koundé] and Eric Garcìa.

"Hopefully some will come back, but we don't know when yet. So I asked Frenkie if he's able to play there; he said 'Yes, when I can help the team I will do it.'

"The same with Brian. I don't know if he ever played [at right-back], maybe in La Masia, but he also played a good level.

"I am happy for him. He deserved these minutes, this game. He is focused, top in training, very professional. This is what we want from him and the players."

Fariñas, 20, looked especially comfortable playing on the same flank as Yamal, someone he played with at youth level.

"You could see he is connected with Lamine," Flick continued. "It's very important. He helped us a lot today playing this position."

The win took Barça back to the top of the table after Atlético Madrid had leapfrogged them earlier on Saturday.

articles.headline: Anthony Gordon, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha on target as Barcelona hit Alavés for six
articles.description: Free-scoring Barcelona put six past Alavés as they bounced back from defeat against Real Madrid in style.
articles.body:
Free-scoring Barcelona put six past Alavés as they bounced back from defeat against Real Madrid in style.

A 2-1 loss to their rivals last time out represented their first dropped points of the season but it was back to business as usual as the table toppers thumped their visitors 6-1 at the Nou Camp.

There were two goals apiece for Raphinha and Lamine Yamal, as well as one from Fermín López and a late topper from England's Anthony Gordon coming off the bench. Mariano Díaz grabbed the late consolation for the Basque outfit.

Hansi Flick was without a handful of first-teamers, including Jules Koundé, Eric García, Andreas Christensen, Dani Olmo, Roony Bardghji, and Xavi Espart, but their collective absence was barely noticed as they made an emphatic start.

Lopez was straight into his work, driving through the defensive line and laying on a simple chance for Raphinha to slot home after just eight minutes.

Abde Rebbach was off target when he had an early opportunity to return fire and the gulf in quality showed when Lopez doubled the lead with a fiery finish. Cutting into the penalty area on the right he read a pass from Yamal then rifled powerfully across Antonio Sivera from a tight angle.

There were already signs of damage limitation by the time Sivera made a wonderful save from Yamal but that merely delayed further pain. Lopez once again found himself at the heart of things, sniping possession in midfield and unleashing Raphinha with a beautifully weighted pass.

The Brazilian let the ball run to the edge of the area then unleashed a precision left-foot finish. With seconds to go before the half-time whistle, the hosts showcased their dominance again, stroking a long sequence of passes in the final third before Yamal pulled the trigger with a bullet of a first-time finish.

With an hour gone and the urgency abating, Gabriel Jesus entered the fray and laid on Barca's fifth with a neat touch. Yamal's delicate flicked finish was initially chalked off for offside flag, but replays overruled the flag.

Barca were not satisfied yet, rounding out their night's work through another of Flick's replacements. Gordon was the beneficiary of a defence-splitting ball from Rodri, with the former Newcastle winger charging down on goal then lifting his shot calmly over the keeper for his first league goal.

But the last word went to a former Real man, with Diaz taking advantage of some slack defending in stoppage time as he went clear and caught Joan García flat-footed.
